title: CUDA/NCCL crossover compatibility experiment log
body:
Purpose:
This document captures an experimental runbook and observed results for cross-version compatibility between NVIDIA driver versions, CUDA, NCCL, and Kubernetes components as part of the private (VPC/on-prem) upgrade work. The goal is to build deterministic validation steps and concrete Terraform module knobs to reduce incidents during rolling upgrades.

Scope & constraints:
- Hardware: H100, A100, T4 nodes present across two clusters (edge and core).
- Kernel: CentOS/Ubuntu variants: 5.15.x, 6.1.x-rc1 kernels in lab staging.
- Container runtime: containerd 1.7.x primarily; one node kept with dockerd for comparison.
- K8s: 1.26 and 1.27 clusters in staging.
- Focus: driver (nvidia-driver), CUDA toolkit (11.8, 12.1, 12.2), NCCL (2.14.x, 2.18.x), and k8s-device-plugin behavior.

High level takeaways (short):
- NV driver 535+ works with CUDA 12.x on H100 in most cases but NCCL 2.14 shows cross-run instability on multiprocessive all-reduce with mixed GPUs (A100+H100) unless NV peer-to-peer and IB firmware are aligned.
- Kubelet 1.27+ exposes a timing window where device-plugin restarts cause ephemeral pod GPU allocation failures; need a short preDrain delay and verify node resource re-registration in terraform module lifecycle hooks.
- containerd/gvisor differences: the gvisor testbed had slower NVML warmup leading to pod readiness timeouts; include a warmup probe in rollout plan.

Experimental matrix (summary table):
Columns: node_type | driver | kernel | cuda | nccl | k8s | runtime | verdict | notes
- H100-standard | 535.86 | 6.1.12 | 12.1 | 2.18.3 | 1.27 | containerd | pass | stable single-node perf
- A100-batch | 515.76 | 5.15.0 | 11.8 | 2.14.3 | 1.26 | containerd | flaky | collect timeout errors under all-reduce
- T4-edge | 470.103 | 5.15.0 | 11.4 | 2.12.10 | 1.26 | dockerd | fail | mismatch: driver too old for CUDA 11.8 images
- mixed-cluster | mixed | mixed | 12.1/11.8 | 2.14-2.18 | 1.27 | containerd | degraded | NCCL PBAR/CONNECT issues under cross-gpu collectives

Detailed run logs (selected runs):
Run 2026-02-22-R1 (staging-core):
- Nodes: 6 x H100 (DGX-like), kernel 6.1.12, driver 535.86, cuda 12.1, nccl 2.18.3, k8s 1.27.0-rc.
- Test: multi-replica GPT shard training toy workload, all-reduce on 4 GPUs.
- Observation: transient NCCL CONNECT retries ~1-2 / 10 minutes across replicas after node reboots. NVPeer2Peer reports OK; IB link flaps coincide with errors.
- Artifact: /var/log/nvidia/pulses-2026-02-22.log (attached in Jira).
- Action: Re-run with 2.18.4-rc -> eliminated CONNECT retries.

Run 2026-01-14-R4 (edge-mix):
- Nodes: 2 x A100 + 2 x H100, driver set on A100 to 515.76, H100 on 535.86, cuda images pinned to 11.8 and 12.1.
- Test: NCCL unbalanced allreduce (hetero shapes).
- Observation: Job making progress but with sporadic hangs; profiling showed inter-device P2P fallback triggered when bitmask mismatch in nvpeer2peer.
- Root cause hypothesis: driver version differences between nodes trigger different topologies (p2p capability bits), which cascades into NCCL choosing suboptimal rings.
- Mitigation: standardize driver families across mixed clusters or force NCCL_TOPO_CONFIG to a conservative topology, but latter hurts perf.

Terraform module notes (practical knobs to add):
- add variable: nvidia_driver_family (string) -> allow module to pick driver package family and pin major version rather than exact patch. Document recommended families per GPU class.
- lifecycle hook: pre_drain_wait_seconds (int) default 30 -> ensures device-plugin re-init and NVML warmup.
- post_install_verification (bool) default true -> trigger k8s job that queries device status (nvidia-smi, nvml, small CUDA kernel run) and waits for N seconds success. Fail early if mismatch.
- rolling_update_max_unavailable_gpus (int) default 1 -> ensure at most one GPU-equivalent worth of capacity is taken offline at a time.
- taint_on_driver_update (bool) -> automatically taint nodes during driver upgrade and coordinate with rollout controller.

Suggested upgrade playbook (staging template):
1) preflight: run 'infra/terraform plan' with nvidia_driver_family pin, collect expected packages.
2) prewarm: execute a node-level job that runs a 10s CUDA vector add per GPU (image: cuda:12.1-runtime) and reports readiness.
3) cordon -> wait pre_drain_wait_seconds -> drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data but keep a custom label 'gpu-upgrade=true' to avoid scheduling other disruptive pods.
4) install driver package -> reboot (if required) -> wait for device-plugin to reregister.
5) run post_install_verification job; if fails, rollback via terraform apply with previous driver_family tag and uncordon.
6) monitor 30m for NCCL/connectivity anomalies with a test workload.

Failure modes and rollback triggers (explicit):
- If post_install_verification fails on >1 node in a single AZ -> automatically mark upgrade aborted and revert with previous AMI/driver.
- If job-level NCCL connect retries >3/sec sustained for 5m across >25% pods -> abort and roll back.
- If device-plugin pod restarts occur >2 per node in 15m -> pause rollout and escalate to SRE.

New test additions to CI infra (small, runnable):
- k8s job: gpu-warmup-check (image: nvidia/cuda:12.1-base) runs: nvidia-smi; /usr/local/cuda/samples/1_Utilities/deviceQuery; small allreduce using nccl-tests with -b 8 -e 256M -f 2 -g 4 for 30s.
- perf gate: 95th pct latency for deviceQuery < 1.5s, nccl-tests throughput within 80% of baseline.

Notes for SRE/Field engineers:
- Keep A/B groups homogeneous in driver family. Mixing is possible but operationally expensive. For greenfield, prefer driver family that covers your highest-capacity GPU (H100) and backport compatibility notes for older GPUs.
- IB firmware mismatches commonly surface as NCCL timeouts; maintain an IB firmware matrix per vendor in asset inventory and include it in upgrade checklist.
- If you rely on node-level kernel lockdown (e.g., grsecurity), validate module signing for nvidia modules; some kernels require explicit module signing steps.

Appendix: short troubleshooting snippets
- device-plugin diagnostic command:
  kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset --tail=200
- verify NVML from inside pod:
  kubectl run -it --rm --restart=Never --image=nvidia/cuda:12.1-base debug-nvml -- nvidia-smi -a
- sample CUDA warmup run in job YAML (wrap in terraform as post_install_verification):
  command: ["/bin/sh","-c","/usr/local/cuda/samples/bin/x86_64/linux/release/deviceQuery || exit 1"]

Raw excerpt (kernel message around a flaky run):
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=4725 Thu Feb 22 14:12:01 2026
[  123.456792] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.

Next steps / open items:
- Add the terraform variables above and run a canary upgrade against a 2-node test pool (target date: 2026-03-20).
- Flesh out IB firmware matrix; assign owner (Marco).
- Add gpu-warmup-check into the Jenkins/CI pipeline and wire alerts for perf gates (Priya).
- Draft an ops runbook for mixed-cluster deployments (Lina).

If you take anything from this log: treat driver-family selection as a primary design decision, and bake warmup + post-install validation into your terraform lifecycle.

End of log.
